question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: a HEAD with user-agent public-agents-ci and accept */*, which is the pair the Public Agents registry's link gate sends to a page (src/lib/net.ts defaults); no cookie, no Authorization header, the fourth request this container made to deepwiki.com in this session

headers.x-vercel-challenge-token: present (a 2.<timestamp>.60.<base64>.<hex> token; the value is in the artifact)

decoded.what-it-answered: HTTP/2 429, content-type text/html, server Vercel, x-vercel-mitigated challenge, a challenge token, and no retry-after. A HEAD carries no body; the GET three minutes earlier with a Chrome user-agent carried a 33,944-byte HTML body titled "Vercel Security Checkpoint".
decoded.the-status-line-read: the origin's status is the SECOND HTTP line in the artifact; this container's egress proxy answers CONNECT with its own HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established first.
decoded.what-a-browser-gets: a real Chromium from this container at 06:03:17Z loaded the same URL and titled it "DeepWiki | AI documentation you can talk to, for every repo". The page is there; what a non-browser caller receives is a challenge.
decoded.the-same-answer-four-times-here-and-six-: this container's three requests at 06:02:49Z, 06:02:52Z and 06:02:55Z (HEAD and GET as the gate, GET as Chrome) and this one all answered 429 with x-vercel-mitigated challenge; the registry's merger reported 6 of 6 from another container on 2026-10-01 between 22:11:49Z and 22:12:03Z with the gate's user-agent and a browser's. Ten readings of one answer across eight hours and two containers is not a rate; what it is, is consistent.
decoded.what-changed-since-september: the artifact this record appends to holds, in its section 9, a GET of https://deepwiki.com/.well-known/public-agents.json on 2026-09-26 at about 06:14Z from the same kind of container that answered HTTP 200 with the application's HTML. So the host served non-browser callers on 2026-09-26 and challenges them on 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02; when between those dates it changed is not measured.
decoded.what-this-is-not-about: the tool. DeepWiki's agent surface is https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp, measured keyless and answering on 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-26 (p-20260926-deepwiki-mcp-unauthenticated); this record is about the homepage, which the registry lists and its link gate fetches nightly. The MCP endpoint was not re-asked today and nothing here says whether it is behind the same challenge.
decoded.why-this-record-exists: the registry's nightly link audit of 2026-10-01 reported this URL dead on this 429, because the gate's page table read 429 as death while its handshake table read it as an answer about the caller (issue #153, pull request #212). The reading that made the gate's verdict wrong belongs in the evidence layer, dated, beside the fix.
decoded.not-measured: whether the challenge is keyed on the user-agent, the address or the absence of a cookie; the three user-agents tried all drew it. Whether a retry-after ever accompanies it (none did). Whether the challenge is a rate limit at all: the first request of the session drew it, so a count of zero prior requests was enough.

finding: A HEAD of https://deepwiki.com/ with the user-agent and accept header the Public Agents registry's link gate sends answers HTTP 429 with server Vercel and x-vercel-mitigated: challenge, no retry-after, on 2026-10-02 at 06:13:40Z, the fourth of four requests from this container to answer the same way within eleven minutes (HEAD and GET with the gate's user-agent, GET with a Chrome user-agent, this HEAD); the registry's merger read 6 of 6 the same from another container on 2026-10-01. A real Chromium loads the page under its own title, so the URL is there and the 429 is a bot challenge delivered as a rate-limit status: an answer about the caller, not about the path. The same host answered a non-browser GET of its well-known path with HTTP 200 on 2026-09-26 (section 9 of the artifact), so the challenge is a change since then, dated to within that window and no tighter. This is the reading on which the registry's nightly link audit of 2026-10-01 called the URL dead (issue #153). It says nothing about DeepWiki's MCP endpoint, which was not asked today, and nothing about what the challenge is keyed on: ten readings of one answer are consistent, not a rate.
